coverage.definition: Pooled node coverage: covered distinct non-seed nodes summed over replays / distinct non-seed observed nodes summed over replays. A node appearing in two replays counts once per replay (denominators are per-replay by construction).

delay_accuracy.definition: Delay accuracy is graded ONLY on non-seed steps where observed_delay_d > 0 (quantified) AND the node was predicted: HIT if the observed delay is within [0.5x, 2x] of the predicted delay for that node, else MISS. The predicted delay for a node is the FIRST-HIT delay: the delay_d of the node's first event in stream order, excluding delay-0 cost-channel leaves (the estimator the harness backtest.py uses; an legacy grading used the maximum delay_d over all events at the node, so its figures are not comparable — a legacy-grading comparison computed on the same runs is published alongside the headline). Grading is deduplicated BY NODE: one graded step per node per replay, the earliest observed step for the node (first in dataset order); later quantified steps at an already-graded node are duplicates — counted, listed, and in no denominator. mean_abs_error_d is the mean of |observed - predicted| over the graded steps only. Quantified non-seed steps at unpredicted nodes have no predicted delay to grade against: they are genuine misses, listed individually, and excluded from the mean. Steps with observed_delay_d = 0 are 'effect observed, delay unquantified': counted in node coverage, excluded from delay grading, and listed.

false_positives.definition: False positives = nodes the engine predicted (cost-only nodes excluded — see cost_leaf_exclusion) with no observed effect at all; an observed step at the seed node counts as an observed effect for this purpose. Listed by node; they are not graded as misses of observed steps.

legacy_grading.label: Legacy grading rules (max-over-events estimator, no node dedupe, delay-0 cost leaves counted as predictions) computed on the SAME engine runs — for continuity only; NOT comparable to the headline grading.

statistics.method: Confidence intervals are exact Clopper-Pearson 95% intervals for a binomial proportion, computed on the pooled counts (coverage: covered / distinct non-seed observed nodes; delay hit rate: hits / graded steps). Baseline: a naive directed k-hop neighbourhood of the seed node over the graph's directed edges, expanded whole hop levels at a time until its non-seed node count first reaches the engine's predicted non-seed node count for the same replay (same events, same node budget); baseline coverage and precision (covered / predicted) are printed beside the engine's, per replay and pooled, and the scorecard states plainly when the engine does not beat the baseline on a metric.

honesty_caveats: Edge shares are MODELED allocations pending re-derivation from PortWatch/Comtrade/CPPI/LSCI: the graph's edge capacity_share and transit values were allocated by the dataset builders, not extracted from those sources, so every predicted delay inherits that modeling choice.

Predicted delays scale with the effective disruption duration: the duration used for each replay is the dataset's stated expected_duration_d, mapped explicitly (see each replay's section). For Red Sea 2024 that stated duration (559 d) is an observed lower bound — days from onset to the last timeline observation, with the disruption still unresolved — not a forecast.
LA 2021 capacity_loss is a MODELED assumption, not a sourced figure (see the LA section, which prints the full basis alongside the LA numbers).
This decomposed presentation refines the raw window-rule rate; it does not change the grading rule v1 used for live Ledger entries.

Engine model (revision 2): lost flow is aggregated in absolute terms over each node's inbound edges; delays are service-time waits from stored backlog — backlog = shortfall x inbound flow x duration, stored capped by the node's real queue_cap, cleared at the spare service rate capacity x (1 - utilisation); one continuous delay function serves queue and congestion; model constants live in the versioned registry. Utilisation is a global registry ASSUMPTION (0.85) — the graph carries no per-node utilisation field — so every wait inherits it. Per-node outcomes are in the tables above; no node-level narrative is reused from engine v1.

IN-SAMPLE: the engine rules were configured with sight of these replay results — the backlog model was adjusted against this same three-episode replay set. This scorecard is therefore an in-sample fit check on three known episodes, not a held-out evaluation, and its figures must not be quoted as out-of-sample accuracy.

LA 2021 is doubly in-sample: its capacity_loss input (0.78) is derived from the same MESocal 10 Nov 2021 snapshot that supplies the LA observed steps' labels, so the LA run is partly graded against its own input source.

DEFERRED: the full 25-event protocol v2 is a roadmap item and has NOT been run. This scorecard grades the 3 shipped replay episodes only; no 25-event held-out protocol stands behind any figure printed here.

methodology.cost_leaf_exclusion: Cost-leaf exclusion: an event on the 'cost' channel with delay_d = 0 is a cost-pressure leaf, not a delay prediction. A node whose only predicted events are delay-0 cost leaves counts as NOT predicted: it earns no coverage credit and is not a false positive. Such nodes are listed per replay as cost-only nodes. Cost leaves never supply a node's first-hit delay.

methodology.determinism: This artifact embeds no timestamp (deliberate). Generating the scorecard twice from the same datasets and graph yields byte-identical scorecard.json and scorecard.md. Anchors: graph hash, per-dataset SHA-256 of the raw file bytes, per-replay run_id and event stream hash.
methodology.effective_spec: Each replay is run on an effective disruption built from the dataset's stated spec: the stated capacity_loss is passed explicitly and the dataset's expected_duration_d (the disruption spec field) is mapped to the engine's duration_d. Every mapping or default substitution is recorded in the replay's disclosures and printed alongside its numbers; the duration used and the capacity_loss basis are stated for every replay. No silent defaults.
methodology.evidence_rule: Evidence rule, enforced in this grading path: an observed step with no evidence source (no evidence_source / evidence_url / evidence provenance) is UNGRADEABLE — never a hit, never a miss, and never silently dropped. Ungradeable steps are counted and listed as their own line per replay and in the aggregate, and are excluded from node coverage, delay grading, and the false-positive comparison (an evidence-less observation is not an observed effect), so every denominator covers evidence-backed steps only.
methodology.false_positives: False positives = nodes the engine predicted (cost-only nodes excluded — see cost_leaf_exclusion) with no observed effect at all; an observed step at the seed node counts as an observed effect for this purpose. Listed by node; they are not graded as misses of observed steps.
methodology.miss_classification: Every observed step carries exactly one class: 'ungradeable' (no evidence source — see evidence_rule; checked first, before any other class), 'seed-input' (at the disruption node), 'unquantified' (non-seed, observed_delay_d = 0), 'duplicate' (non-seed, quantified, at a node already graded in this replay — see the dedupe rule in delay_accuracy), or 'genuine' (non-seed, quantified, first step at its node). Genuine misses — graded steps outside the [0.5x, 2x] window plus quantified steps at unpredicted nodes — are listed individually with observed vs predicted values.
methodology.node_coverage: Node coverage = (distinct non-seed nodes with at least one observed effect that the engine predicted) / (distinct non-seed nodes with at least one observed effect). 'Predicted' means at least one event at the node that is not a delay-0 cost-channel leaf (see cost_leaf_exclusion). Covered and uncovered nodes are listed.
methodology.seed_exclusion: Observed steps at the replay disruption's own node are the scenario input, not predictions. They are excluded from all grading and are counted and listed separately as input steps.

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: MODELED assumption - not a sourced figure and never to be presented as one. No sourced capacity-loss fraction exists for LA 2021: the source record quantifies queues and waits, not capacity loss, and berth throughput did not collapse (the Port of Los Angeles was on track for a record ~10.7M TEU in 2021, Port of Los Angeles release, 20 Dec 2021), so no throughput-drop derivation is defensible. Model: at the 10 Nov 2021 MESocal snapshot the complex held 109 container ships waiting and 30 at berth; capacity_loss is set to the waiting share of container ships present, 109 / (109 + 30) = 0.78 (rounded to 2 dp) - a stock-share proxy for the share of container-ship flow the berth/landside system was not serving at the peak snapshot, NOT a measured throughput drop. The binding constraint was landside (dwell/driver channel), not berth capacity. Any scorecard printing LA results must print this modeled assumption alongside them. (An earlier version carried capacity_loss as null; the engine then silently substituted its 0.5 default for congestion-kind specs.)

baseline_k_hop.method: Confidence intervals are exact Clopper-Pearson 95% intervals for a binomial proportion, computed on the pooled counts (coverage: covered / distinct non-seed observed nodes; delay hit rate: hits / graded steps). Baseline: a naive directed k-hop neighbourhood of the seed node over the graph's directed edges, expanded whole hop levels at a time until its non-seed node count first reaches the engine's predicted non-seed node count for the same replay (same events, same node budget); baseline coverage and precision (covered / predicted) are printed beside the engine's, per replay and pooled, and the scorecard states plainly when the engine does not beat the baseline on a metric.

capacity_loss_basis.derivation: The loss figure is stated by the source: gross tonnage of ships entering the Gulf of Aden fell >70% between the 1st half of Dec 2023 and the 1st half of Feb 2024; taken as 0.7 (the stated floor). Corroborated in the same timeline by Suez transits -70% by Jun 2024 (UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024). No arithmetic conversion applied. Container-ship capacity fell further (-92% by Jun 2024); 0.7 is the conservative all-shipping figure.

coverage.definition: Node coverage = (distinct non-seed nodes with at least one observed effect that the engine predicted) / (distinct non-seed nodes with at least one observed effect). 'Predicted' means at least one event at the node that is not a delay-0 cost-channel leaf (see cost_leaf_exclusion). Covered and uncovered nodes are listed.

delay_accuracy.definition: Delay accuracy is graded ONLY on non-seed steps where observed_delay_d > 0 (quantified) AND the node was predicted: HIT if the observed delay is within [0.5x, 2x] of the predicted delay for that node, else MISS. The predicted delay for a node is the FIRST-HIT delay: the delay_d of the node's first event in stream order, excluding delay-0 cost-channel leaves (the estimator the harness backtest.py uses; an legacy grading used the maximum delay_d over all events at the node, so its figures are not comparable — a legacy-grading comparison computed on the same runs is published alongside the headline). Grading is deduplicated BY NODE: one graded step per node per replay, the earliest observed step for the node (first in dataset order); later quantified steps at an already-graded node are duplicates — counted, listed, and in no denominator. mean_abs_error_d is the mean of |observed - predicted| over the graded steps only. Quantified non-seed steps at unpredicted nodes have no predicted delay to grade against: they are genuine misses, listed individually, and excluded from the mean. Steps with observed_delay_d = 0 are 'effect observed, delay unquantified': counted in node coverage, excluded from delay grading, and listed.
delay_accuracy.predicted_delay_choice: first-hit delay_d: the node's first event in stream order, excluding delay-0 cost leaves
